action_regex_regex_help:
A regex expression to match the input.

If you use group names in the regex expression Tasker will create a variable for each of those groups. That variable can be accessed either as direct value or as an array if multiple matches are found.
array_join_formatter_help:
Will merge each position of the arrays above with the format you specify here.

Use the original array name as the placeholder in the format

For example, if you have 2 arrays, %names and %ages and use the fomat '%names is %ages years old' it'll join 
'%names(1) is %ages(1) years old'
'%names(2) is %ages(2) years old'
and so on.
array_join_output_help:
Name of the array that will contain the formatted values.

Each position of this array will contain the corresponding positions of all the input arrays joined with the rules above.
array_join_output_joiner_help: If set, will join the resulting array and make the output variable a single value instead of an array.
array_joiner_help:
Will simply merge each position of the arrays above with the joiner.

For example, if you have 2 arrays, %names and %ages and use the joiner ' - ' it'll join '%names(1) - %ages(1)', '%names(2) - %ages(2)' and so on.
array_merge_replace_variables_in_arrays_: If enabled, Tasker will not only replace the array items themselves in, but it will look INSIDE those array items and replace any variables there too.
call_reject_help: Prevent call from going through and disconnects it as if the user had manually rejected it
call_silence_help: Sets whether ringing should be silenced for the incoming call but call will still go through.
call_skip_log_help: Prevent call from going through and make the call not appear in your call log
clipboard_image_help: Setting an image on the clipboard will overwrite the text above
convert_orientation_help: If enabled will convert orientation values to degrees. Result must have at least 3 values for this to work.
dc_collision_help:
What to do when another copy of this task is already executing.

See the page on Tasks in the Userguide for more information.
dc_delete_on_disable_help: Whether this profile should be deleted when the repeat count gets to 0.
dc_element_geom_help:
Allows more precise specification of the element's position (x,y) and size (width x height) than is possible via finger adjustment.

There is a separate geometry specification for each display orientation (portrait and landscape).
dc_enforce_task_order_help: Ensure that tasks resulting from this profile activation or deactivation remain queued until previous tasks from this profile are complete.
dc_insert_your_google_api_key_check_help: Insert your Google API Key. Check the action's help page for more info.
dc_licence_help: For customers who purchased a direct-download key on or after July 2018:
dc_limit_repeats_help: Whether to limit the number of times the profile can become active e.g. if its enter task should only be run once.
dc_limit_repeats_to_help: The number of times remaining before this profile becomes disabled.
dc_profile_cooldown_help:
The times after the profile has become active before it can again become active.

Cooldown time is reset after a reboot.
dc_profile_priority_help:
The priority of the enter and exit tasks run by this profile.

Note: this does *not* affect the profile becoming active in any way.
dc_profile_properties_restore_settings_h:
Whether to automatically restore the values of any settings (actions marked with a double arrow symbol) changed by this profile when it deactivates.

See also: Settings in the Userguide.
dc_run_exit_on_startup_if_not_active_hel: If this option is enabled, when Tasker starts up (after a reboot for example) the exit task for this profile will be ran if the profile's condition doesn't match your current situation, ie. the profile is not active
dc_show_notification_help_help:
Whether to include this task in the Running Tasks notification that updates every time a task is started or stopped.

You can disable the notification altogether by long-clicking it and changing its settings.
dc_stay_awake_help:
Whether to keep the device running while the task is running. The default is that tasks will be guaranteed to be kept running for around a minute from their start time.

Be careful specifying this option for a task with a loop, it can very quickly drain your battery.
dc_widget_task_priority_help: The priority at which the widget/shortcut task will be launched.
editor_number_format_field_help: Type any format pattern, or pick an example.
help_action_cancel_layout: Ends the screen in error, failing the task waiting on it. The optional message is delivered to the caller as %errmsg.
help_action_clear_variable: Unsets a variable when this event fires, removing its value instead of leaving it blank. If you clear a global variable (any name with an uppercase letter, like %MyVar), it's also cleared at the Tasker level - not just within the screen.
help_action_dismiss_layout: Closes the current layout and returns any output variables to the caller. The output variables come from values set by other event handlers or component states during the layout's lifetime.
help_action_haptic_feedback: Makes the device vibrate briefly to give the user tactile feedback. Choose between a light click, heavy tap, or double tap. Place this before other actions so the user feels it immediately.
help_action_output_to_variable: Captures the data produced by this event and stores it in screen variables. For example, a text input's "text changed" event can save the typed text into a variable.
help_action_run_component_action: Triggers an action on another component by its ID, like reloading a web view or seeking a video. You can optionally capture the action's result into variables.
help_action_run_task: Runs a Tasker task by name and optionally passes variables to it. Use this to trigger any automation you've built in Tasker from within a Scene V2 layout.
help_action_set_variable: Sets a variable to a specific value when this event fires. If you use a global variable (any name with an uppercase letter, like %MyVar), it's also set at the Tasker level - not just within the screen. You can build complex values by mixing text and variables, like "Hello %name! You have %count messages".
help_action_simulate_interaction: Programmatically fires any event handler configured on a target component. eventParams optionally narrows the match (e.g. count=2 for multi_click). outputs optionally supplies values the simulated event would have produced. Visual feedback is not produced; only the configured handlers run.
help_action_stop: Skips the actions after it in this handler. With a condition it only stops when the condition is true, checked when the Stop is reached, so it sees what earlier actions set. Turn on Also stop later handlers to skip the handlers after this one too: for if / else, give each handler a condition and end it with such a Stop, and leave the last handler without a condition so it only runs when none of the others did.
help_action_tasker_command: Sends a named command string to Tasker. Use this for simple, fire-and-forget signals that a Tasker profile or task is listening for.
help_action_toggle_variable: Flips a boolean screen variable to its opposite value. Recognizes truthy values (true, 1, yes, on, 1.0) and falsey values (false, 0, no, off, 0.0). If the variable is unset or unrecognized it is treated as false and toggled to true.
help_adb_wifi_enable_debugging:
Most people don't need debugging to be enabled at all times on their Android devices. It might be a security risk if you accidentally accept an unknown request to start debugging which could put your phone at risk.

By enabling this option you can leave debugging off and the action will enable it when ran and disable it afterwards, leaving your phone "closed down" for the majority of time!
help_adb_wifi_result_encoding:
If you are expecting a result with non-standard characters (like à or é) you can use a different encoding for the result.

Try using 'UTF-8' (no quotes) in situations like this, for example.
help_allow_child_overwrite_vars:
If enabled the child task is free to overwrite any variables that already exist in this parent task.

Please note that you need to enable the option to replace in the 'Return' action as well.

This option is meant to be used with child tasks that you know yourself and not any random child tasks.

Please be aware that if you enable this, child tasks can change the parents local and Project/Profile/Task variables even if Local Variable Passthrough is not checked and the contents of the parent's variables are not visible to the child task.
help_allow_scene_outside_boundaries:
If enabled, will allow the scene to be shown outside normal UI boundaries.

This is necessary to display overlays on the status bar on phones with notches, or on the navigation bar for example.

To display scenes outside boundaries, manually enter the horizontal and vertical positions (using the cross-arrow button on each field) and input appropriate values, including negative ones.

When using this mode any values entered manually (instead of using the seek control) will be in pixels instead of the normal 0-200 range to allow more fine-grained control.
help_aspect_ratio: Aspect ratio for the output image. Providers that don't support this natively get the value injected into the prompt as a fallback.
help_clear_conversation_id: The ID of the conversation to clear. Leave blank to clear ALL conversations.
help_component_arrays_merge_template: Repeats its template once per element of the arrays referenced inside it. Each row is bound live to its own element, so a handler can set or toggle that row's value. No separate array list; the arrays are inferred from the template.
help_component_bottom_app_bar: A horizontal bar at the bottom of the screen for actions and navigation. Use this inside a Scaffold's bottom bar slot. Place icon buttons or text inside for quick access to common actions.
help_component_box: Layers items on top of each other, like stacking sheets of paper. The last item added appears on top. Use this when you want to overlap elements - like putting text over an image or a badge on a corner.
help_component_button: A clickable button with a label. When someone taps it, it can trigger an action like running a task, navigating somewhere, or changing a value.
help_component_camera: Live camera preview using CameraX. Selects a lens by facing and tier (main / wide / tele) with graceful fallback. Requires CAMERA permission from the host app.
help_component_card: A Material 3 container that groups related content with a styled surface. Choose Filled for a flat background, Elevated for a raised look with shadow, or Outlined for a bordered appearance. Children stack vertically inside.
help_component_checkbox: A checkbox that can be checked or unchecked. Use this to let the user toggle an option on or off. Works like a switch but with a checkbox appearance.
help_component_column: Stacks items from top to bottom, one below the other. Use this when you want elements arranged vertically - like a list of settings, messages, or any content that flows downward.
help_component_divider: A thin line that separates sections of content. Use this to visually group related items or break up a long list into distinct parts.
help_component_dropdown: A container with a trigger and a popup content area
help_component_fab: A prominent circular button that floats above the content, used for the primary action on a screen. Use this inside a Scaffold's floating action button slot. Place an icon or text inside to indicate the action.
help_component_flexbox: Flexible container with wrapping, grow/shrink, and CSS-like alignment. Experimental API.
help_component_flow_column: A vertical container that wraps children to the next column when they overflow. Supports spacing, max items per column, max lines, and overflow control.
help_component_flow_row: A horizontal container that wraps children to the next line when they overflow. Supports spacing, max items per row, max lines, and overflow control.
help_component_icon_button: A button with a Material icon inside. Provides a standard 48dp touch target with ripple feedback around a 24dp icon. Use this for toolbar actions, navigation icons, and compact interactive elements.
help_component_image: Shows a picture from a web address or file. You can control how the image is scaled and cropped to fit the available space.
help_component_navigation_bar: A horizontal bar at the bottom of the screen for switching between top-level app destinations. Each item shows an icon and optional label. Place NavigationItem components inside to define the destinations.
help_component_navigation_item: An item inside a Navigation Bar. Displays a Material icon with an optional text label. Supports selected state and configurable label visibility. Must be placed inside a Row parent to render correctly.
help_component_placeholder: A temporary stand-in element that shows where a real component will go. Use this while designing your layout to reserve space before you decide what to put there.
help_component_progress_bar: A progress indicator supporting linear and circular styles with determinate and indeterminate modes. Includes actions for timed animation (count up/down) and fires an event on animation completion.
help_component_range_slider: A Material 3 range slider for selecting a start and end value within a range. Supports continuous or discrete steps. Emits raw values and 0-1 percentages on change.
help_component_row: Places items side by side from left to right. Use this when you want elements arranged horizontally - like a toolbar with buttons, a row of icons, or items that sit next to each other.
help_component_scaffold: A page-level layout with dedicated areas for a top bar, navigation bar, floating action button, and main content. The content area automatically avoids overlapping the bars. Use this to build standard app screens with toolbars and navigation.
help_component_segmented_button_item: A single segment within a Segmented Button Row. Can also be used standalone as a toggle button.
help_component_segmented_button_row: A row of segmented buttons with single or multi selection mode.
help_component_slider: A Material 3 slider for selecting a single value within a range. Supports continuous or discrete steps. Emits the raw value and a 0-1 percentage on change.
help_component_spacer: An invisible empty space used to create gaps between other elements. Use this to add breathing room in your layout without using padding on individual items.
help_component_switch: A toggle that can be turned on or off, like a light switch. Use this to let the user enable or disable something. The current state can be read and changed.
help_component_text: Displays text on screen. You can customize the font, size, color, and alignment. Use this for labels, titles, descriptions, or any written content.
help_component_text_input: A text field where the user can type. Use this for forms, search bars, or any place where you need to collect text from the user. The typed text is stored in a variable.
help_component_top_app_bar: A horizontal bar at the top of the screen with a title, optional navigation icon, and action buttons. Use this inside a Scaffold's top bar slot to create a standard app header.
help_component_variable: Displays the current value of a Tasker variable as text. The content updates automatically whenever the variable changes - useful for showing live data like time, battery level, or sensor readings.
help_component_video: Plays video, animated GIF, or YouTube from a URL, file path, or data URI. YouTube URLs are auto-detected. Supports playback control via actions and fires events for media state changes.
help_component_webview: Renders web content in a native WebView from a URL, local file, or inline HTML (auto-detected). Supports a JavaScript bridge, reactive variables, page events, and actions like reload, find, and zoom.
help_contact_via_app_backout: When enabled, will back out of the opened WhatsApp conversation so you end up where you were before the conversation was opened.
help_continue_task_immediately: If checked, the action returns immediately and the response is delivered via the AI Chat Response event.
help_conversation_id: A name to group turns into a multi-turn chat. Leave blank to send a one-shot turn with no history.
help_cull_older_messages: If checked, dropped messages are deleted along with their attached files.
help_effort: Reasoning effort hint: Default, Low, Medium, High, XHigh, Max. Not all models honor every level.
help_event_conversation_id: Filter by conversation ID. Leave blank to match every conversation.
help_event_only_full_responses: Trigger only when the AI returns its complete response. Leave unchecked to also trigger on intermediate streaming snapshots.
help_files: Comma-separated file paths to attach (images, PDFs, text). Leave blank for none.
help_format_json_overwrite_source: When on (the default), the formatted JSON is written straight back to the variable used in the JSON field above, so this action works as a simple passthrough without you having to use the %fj_formatted output. Has no effect if the JSON field isn't a single plain variable (for example, literal text or a structured reference like %var.key).
help_go_home_package:
This will not change your default launcher. It will simply launch it once. If you touch the home button your default launcher will be opened.

If you want to change the default launcher check out the ADB Wifi action.
help_interactive_out_of_bounds_scenes:
If the Tasker Accessibility Service is enabled when this scene is created and you enable the 'Blocking Overlay +' option below, you'll be able to interact with the scene even if it is on the status bar or navigation bar, meaning that you can create custom buttons for your navigation bar for example!

These scenes will also show on your lock screen and some Always-On-Displays (depending on your phone) and can be interacted with on the lock screen even if the phone is locked!
help_keep_last_x_messages: Keep the last N messages and drop earlier ones. Leave blank or 0 to clear all messages of the conversation.
help_limit_passthrough:
Either a Tasker pattern or a comma separated list to limit which variables can go through.

Local variables that do not match the pattern or comma separated list will not be available in the other task.
help_local_variable_passthrough_limit:
A comma separated list of variable names (including the %) that represent the variables that you want to pass through to the other task.

Other local variables will not be available in the other task.
help_max_messages_in_conversation: Cap the number of stored messages per conversation. Older messages are dropped on save.
help_max_output_tokens: Cap on output token count. Leave blank for the provider default.
help_max_results: Number of images to generate. Defaults to 1.
help_model: The model id (e.g. gemini-2.5-flash). Leave blank to use the provider's default.
help_modifier_alignment: Controls where this element is positioned within its parent container. For example, you can center it, push it to a corner, or align it to the bottom. The available options depend on the parent type.
help_modifier_alpha: Controls how see-through the element is. A value of 1 is fully visible, 0 is completely invisible. Use this to fade elements in or out, or to make background elements partially transparent.
help_modifier_aspect_ratio: Forces the element to a fixed width-to-height ratio (1 = square). Inside a container that gives it bounded space, it grows to the largest size that keeps the ratio and fits. Great for a square that scales to any screen.
help_modifier_background: Fills the area behind the element with a color. Use this to highlight sections, create colored cards, or give any element a visible backdrop.
help_modifier_blur: Applies a Gaussian blur effect to the element. Requires Android 12 (API 31) or higher.
help_modifier_border: Draws a visible outline around the element. Like a border on a web page, it takes up space: the content is moved inward by the border's thickness. You can set the line thickness, color, and corner rounding. On a rectangle, turn off Uniform to give each side its own thickness (0 hides that side), for example to draw only a line under a row. Use this to frame content, highlight selections, or create outlined buttons.
help_modifier_clip: Crops the element to a shape - like rounded corners or a circle. Any content that falls outside the shape is hidden. Use this to create rounded cards, circular profile pictures, or pill-shaped buttons.
help_modifier_container_color: Sets the fill color of a Button, Icon Button, Floating Action Button, app bar, Navigation Bar or Scaffold, replacing its own container color. Has no effect on other elements (use Background there). Add several with Apply When conditions to change colors from a variable; when more than one applies, the last one wins.
help_modifier_content_color: Sets the color of text and icons in this element and everything inside it that doesn't set its own color. On a Text, Image, Icon Button, Button, Floating Action Button, app bar, Navigation Bar or Scaffold it also replaces that element's own text, tint or content color. Add several with Apply When conditions to change colors from a variable; when more than one applies, the last one wins.
help_modifier_fill_height: Makes the element stretch to fill all available vertical space. The width stays based on the content. Use this for sidebars or elements that should be as tall as their container.
help_modifier_fill_size: Makes the element stretch to fill all the space its parent offers, in both width and height. Because the element claims all that space, a parent that would otherwise be measured by its content (like a Box) is pushed to the full available size too. Use it when the element really should take over the whole area. To be exactly as big as the Box you're in without making that Box any bigger, use "Match Parent Size" instead.
help_modifier_fill_width: Makes the element stretch to fill all available horizontal space. The height stays based on the content. Use this for items that should span the full width, like a banner or a full-width button.
help_modifier_flex: Controls grow, shrink, basis, alignment, and order inside a FlexBox.
help_modifier_horizontal_scroll: Lets the content inside scroll left and right when it's wider than the visible area. Use this for wide content like a timeline, image gallery, or a row of cards that extends beyond the screen.
help_modifier_marquee: Scrolls the element horizontally when it overflows its container, creating a marquee/ticker effect. Configure the number of loops, scroll speed, and spacing between repetitions.
help_modifier_match_parent_size: Makes the element exactly as big as the Box it's in, without influencing how big that Box becomes: the Box is still measured by its other elements. Use it for a background or overlay layer that should match whatever the other elements inside the Box need. Only works directly inside a Box, and only if at least one other element there isn't using it. To instead stretch to all the available space, and let the parent grow with it, use "Full Size".
help_modifier_offset: Shifts the element from its normal position by a set amount horizontally or vertically. The space it originally occupied stays reserved. Use this for fine-tuning placement or creating overlapping effects.
help_modifier_padding: Adds empty space inside the element's edges, pushing the content inward. Think of it like the space between a picture frame and the picture itself. You can set different amounts for each side.
help_modifier_rotate: Spins the element by a number of degrees. Use this to tilt text, create angled decorations, or rotate images. The element rotates around its center point.
help_modifier_scale: Stretches or squashes the element's rendered pixels on each axis. Values above 1 enlarge, below 1 shrink, negative flip. The element's layout size does not change - add a Padding modifier above this one if you need to reserve space for the overflow. Useful for distortion effects on text or images.
help_modifier_shadow: Adds a drop shadow behind the element, giving it a raised appearance. You can control the shadow's size, blur, and color. Use this to make cards or buttons look elevated above the background.
help_modifier_size: Sets the exact width and height of the element. Use this when you need an element to be a precise, fixed size regardless of its content or screen size.
help_modifier_size_in: Sets minimum and maximum limits for the element's width and height. The element can grow or shrink within these bounds. Use this when you want flexible sizing with guaranteed limits.
help_modifier_vertical_scroll: Lets the content inside scroll up and down when it's taller than the visible area. Use this when you have more content than fits on screen - like a long list or a lengthy form.
help_modifier_weight: Controls how much of the available space this element gets compared to its neighbors. An element with weight 2 gets twice the space of one with weight 1. Only works inside Rows and Columns.
help_modifier_window_drag: Makes the element act as a drag handle for the overlay window. When the user drags this element, the entire overlay window moves with their finger. Only useful when the scene is shown as an overlay.
help_negative_prompt: Things to avoid in the output. Providers that don't support this natively get the value injected into the prompt as a fallback.
help_notify_plain_icon_can_be_anything:
The notification icon that shows in the status bar at the top of your display.

This icon can be any built-in icon, local file, URL, a Material Symbol (with configurable weight, fill, grade and optical size) or even just some text.

For example, you could create a notification with '26º' set as the icon and that text would appear on your status bar.
help_notify_plain_live_update:
Only available on Android 16+.

Will only show if Tasker is not the foreground app.

Live Update notifications appear more prominently on system surfaces, including at the top of the notification drawer and the lock screen, and as a chip in the status bar.
help_notify_short_critical_text:
Only available on Android 16+.

Will only show if Tasker is not the foreground app.

Sets a very short string summarizing the most critical information contained in the notification. Suggested max length is 7 characters, and there is no guarantee how much or how little of this text will be shown.

If shown, will appear in the Notification Icon Chip if 'Live Update' is enabled, and only if Tasker is not in the foreground.
help_output_file_name: Optional base filename (without extension). When more than one image is generated, _N suffixes are appended.
help_output_folder_chat: Folder to save any output files (e.g. images returned by multimodal models). Leave blank to use the cache directory.
help_output_folder_image: Folder to save the generated images. Required.
help_override_api_key: Optional API key to use just for this call. Overrides the saved key for the chosen provider.
help_perform_task_passthrough: If enabled all the variables that are available in this task will also be available in the child task according to the restrictions below.
help_pick_input_text: Will appear in the dialog if the title is also set
help_pick_input_title: If set will make a dialog appear prior to picking the input with the title and text, unless the specific input picker has a place for the title (like the Time dialog for example).
help_pick_matter_device:
You can control multiple devices in a single action using Tasker's Pattern Matching.

For example, if you have a light called 'Ceiling 1' and another one called 'Ceiling 2', you can toggle them both by setting the name to 'Ceiling *'.

All options bellow will apply to all matching devices.
help_progress_action:
Whether to show/update a progress dialog or to hide an existing one.

If you choose to hide the dialog but the dialog isn't showing the action will end successfully right away.
help_progress_animation_frame_duration: The time in milliseconds that each image appears on the screen
help_progress_animation_images: A list of images to use as an animation in the dialog.
help_progress_animation_tint:
This will tint the images with the selected color where they are not transparent.

By default this is set to Tasker's accent color
help_progress_title_text:
You must set this if the dialog isn't already showing.

If it's already showing you can omit this and the last used value will be kept.
help_progress_type: You can either show a looping animation if you don't have a numeric progress to report, or show a progress bar where you can show numerical progress.
help_provider: The AI provider to use (e.g. Gemini, Claude). Leave blank to use the active provider from the AI screen.
help_return_passthrough: If enabled all the variables that are available in this task will also be available in the parent task according to the restrictions below.
help_return_passthrough_list: If you only want to send a few variables back to the parent task, insert a / separated list of those variable names here.
help_return_passthrough_replace:
If this is not enabled, variables that already have a value on the parent task will not be replaced by their values in this task.

Please note that you need to enable the option to allow replacements in the 'Perform Task' action as well.
help_run_shell_use_shizuku:
You can run a command with Shizuku, meaning that the command will use whatever privileges Shizuku has on your device.

To use this, the Shizuku service has to be running and Tasker has to have the Shizuku permission enabled.
help_run_shell_use_tasker_settings:
Since Tasker started targeting API 30 some shell commands (like "ip neigh") stopped working.

Use this option to use the Tasker Settings app to run the command instead of it running directly in Tasker.
help_screen_capture_mode:
You can either start, stop or query a screen capture.

Starting a capture when it's already started will result in an error.

Stopping a capture when it's already stopped will result in an error.

Use 'Query' to know if a capture is currently ongoing or not (check the %sc_is_capturing variable).
help_seed: Optional integer seed for reproducible generation. Not all providers honor this.
help_set_quick_tile_command:
An optional Tasker command that will be sent on tap.

You can react to this command in a profile with the 'Tasker Command' event condition.
help_set_quick_tile_command_prefix:
If set, instead of just sending the commands set above, all commands will be prefixed with the prefix set here followed by '=:='.

For example, if you set the regular command to 'short', the long click command to 'long' and the prefix to 'quick', on normal tap the 'quick=:=short' command will be sent and on long tap the 'quick=:=long' command will be sent.
help_set_quick_tile_icon:
The icon for the quick setting tile.

If not set, the task's icon will be used instead.

You can also use any text characters as it'll use that as an icon although be aware that at max only 1 or 2 characters will fit in the small icon's size.

You can also pick a Material Symbol: its fill follows the tile's state (filled when active, outline when inactive).
help_set_quick_tile_label:
The label for the quick setting tile.

If not set, the task's name will be used instead.
help_show_on_lock_screen_everywhere:
Will make an overlay scene show on the lock screen and over the notification tray.

If you run this action with this option enabled and the Tasker accessibility service is not running an error notification will be shown and the action will error out.
help_show_on_lock_screen_interactive_eve:
Will make an overlay scene show (and be interactive) on the lock screen and on some devices even in the Always-On-Display.

It'll also make scenes clickable even if they are on the status or notification bars

If you run this action with this option enabled and the Tasker accessibility service is not running an error notification will be shown and the action will error out.

Useful if you want to show a blocking overlay that is interactive even if on the status/navigation bar and lock screen.

If this option is not enabled the scene will not show on the lock screen and won't be clickable if it's over the status/navigation bar.
help_streaming_variable: Optional global variable name to update with the response as it streams (debounced).
help_sv2_auto_dismiss_ms: Automatically dismiss the overlay after this many milliseconds. Set to 0 or leave empty to keep the overlay visible until you dismiss it manually with the "Scene v2 Dismiss" action.
help_sv2_blocking: When enabled, the overlay blocks touches from passing through to the apps behind it. When disabled, you can still interact with other apps through the overlay.
help_sv2_continue_task_immediately: When enabled, the task continues running immediately after showing the scene without waiting for a result. When disabled, the task pauses until the scene is dismissed and returns its result values.
help_sv2_dismiss_animation: The animation played when the overlay is dismissed. Choose "None" for the overlay to disappear instantly.
help_sv2_dismiss_screen_id: The Screen ID of the scene to dismiss. This should match the Screen ID used when the scene was shown. If left empty, all currently visible V2 scenes will be dismissed.
help_sv2_display_id: The ID of the physical display to show this scene on. If left empty, the primary display is used. Use the magnifying glass to pick from connected displays.
help_sv2_display_mode:
How the scene should be displayed on screen.

• Fullscreen: takes up the entire screen like a regular app
• Dialog: appears as a floating window in the center of the screen
• Overlay: floats on top of other apps and can be positioned anywhere
help_sv2_drag_off_screen: If on, the overlay can be dragged partially off any edge of the screen and stays where you leave it. If off, the overlay is kept fully on screen while being dragged. Only applies to overlays.
help_sv2_element_id: The ID of the element to update. Each element in a scene has a unique ID. Use the magnifying glass to pick from the elements in one of your scenes.
help_sv2_execute_action_name: The name of the action to execute on the component (e.g. "focus"). Different component types support different actions. Use the magnifying glass to see available actions for a specific component.
help_sv2_execute_element_id: The ID of the component to send the action to. The component must be currently rendered (visible) in the active scene. Use the magnifying glass to pick from elements in one of your scenes.
help_sv2_execute_param_names: Optional comma-separated parameter names for the action. Must have the same number of elements as Values. Use the magnifying glass to browse available parameter names for the selected action.
help_sv2_execute_param_values: Optional comma-separated parameter values corresponding to the Names field. Must have the same number of elements as Names. You can use Tasker arrays directly in this field.
help_sv2_execute_screen_id: The Screen ID of the scene containing the component you want to send an action to. This should match the Screen ID used when the scene was shown.
help_sv2_get_element_id: The ID of the element to read the current value from. For example, a TextInput element's current text, or a Switch element's checked state.
help_sv2_get_screen_id: The Screen ID of the scene to read values from. This should match the Screen ID used when the scene was shown.
help_sv2_height: The height of the overlay in dp (e.g. 400) or as a percentage of screen height (e.g. 50%). If left empty, the overlay will automatically size itself to fit its content. For different values per orientation, use "portrait,landscape" (e.g. 300,500).
help_sv2_long_click_root_to_dismiss: When enabled, long-pressing anywhere on the overlay will dismiss it. This adds a temporary dismiss handler to the root component at runtime without modifying the scene definition.
help_sv2_name_or_json: The name of a Scene V2 that you have created. Use the magnifying glass to pick from your existing scenes. You can also paste raw JSON layout code here if you want to show a scene that isn't saved.
help_sv2_overlay_blocking: Change whether the overlay blocks touches. Leave unchecked to keep the current setting.
help_sv2_overlay_height: The new height for the overlay in dp. Leave empty to keep the current height. For different values per orientation, use "portrait,landscape" (e.g. 300,500).
help_sv2_overlay_screen_id: The Screen ID of the overlay to update. This should match the Screen ID used when the overlay was shown.
help_sv2_overlay_transition_animation: The animation to use when moving or resizing the overlay to its new position/size.
help_sv2_overlay_transition_duration_ms: How long the transition animation takes, in milliseconds.
help_sv2_overlay_transition_easing: The acceleration curve for the transition animation.
help_sv2_overlay_width: The new width for the overlay in dp. Leave empty to keep the current width. For different values per orientation, use "portrait,landscape" (e.g. 300,500).
help_sv2_overlay_x_position: The new horizontal position for the overlay, in dp. Leave empty to keep the current position. For different values per orientation, use "portrait,landscape" (e.g. 300,500).
help_sv2_overlay_y_position: The new vertical position for the overlay, in dp. Leave empty to keep the current position. For different values per orientation, use "portrait,landscape" (e.g. 300,500).
help_sv2_property: The name of the property to change on the element. Different element types have different properties (for example, a Text element has "text", "textSize", "color"). Use the magnifying glass to see available properties for a specific element.
help_sv2_show_animation: The animation played when the overlay first appears on screen. Choose "None" for the overlay to appear instantly.
help_sv2_show_over_everything: When enabled, the overlay uses the accessibility service to display over everything, including the lock screen and system dialogs. Requires the Tasker accessibility service to be enabled.
help_sv2_show_screen_id: An optional identifier for this scene instance. If you show the same scene multiple times, each one needs a different Screen ID so you can update or dismiss them independently. If left empty, the scene name is used as the Screen ID.
help_sv2_timeout_ms: Maximum time to wait for the scene to be dismissed, in milliseconds. If the scene is not dismissed within this time, the action will fail. Set to 0 to wait indefinitely.
help_sv2_transition_animation: The animation used when the overlay moves or resizes (for example, when you update its position with "Scene v2 Update Overlay"). Choose "None" for instant changes.
help_sv2_transition_duration_ms: How long transition animations take, in milliseconds. The default is 400ms. Lower values make transitions faster; higher values make them slower and smoother.
help_sv2_transition_easing: The acceleration curve for transition animations. This controls whether the animation starts slow and speeds up, starts fast and slows down, or moves at a constant speed.
help_sv2_trigger_element_id: The ID of the element whose event handlers should fire. The element must be currently visible in the active scene. Use the magnifying glass to pick from elements in one of your scenes.
help_sv2_trigger_event_id: The event to trigger (e.g. "click", "hold", "multi_click", "text_changed"). All handlers on the element listening for this event will run. The action fails if the element has no handler for it. Use the magnifying glass to pick from the events configured on the chosen element.
help_sv2_trigger_event_output_names: Optional comma-separated output names supplied to the fired handler as if the event had produced them (e.g. "text"). Must have the same number of elements as Event Output Values.
help_sv2_trigger_event_output_values: Optional comma-separated output values corresponding to Event Output Names (e.g. "hello"). You can use Tasker arrays directly. Must have the same number of elements as Event Output Names.
help_sv2_trigger_event_param_names: Optional comma-separated names used to pick a specific handler when several listen for the same event (e.g. "count" for multi_click). Must have the same number of elements as Event Param Values.
help_sv2_trigger_event_param_values: Optional comma-separated values matched against the corresponding Event Param Names (e.g. "2"). Must have the same number of elements as Event Param Names.
help_sv2_trigger_screen_id: The Screen ID of the scene containing the element whose event you want to trigger. Must match the Screen ID used when the scene was shown.
help_sv2_update_screen_id: The Screen ID of the scene containing the element you want to update. This should match the Screen ID used when the scene was shown.
help_sv2_value: The new value to set for the property. What you enter here depends on the property: for "text" it would be the new text to display, for "color" it would be a color value like "#FF0000" or a theme color name.
help_sv2_wait_screen_id: The Screen ID of the scene to wait for. This should match the Screen ID used when the scene was shown. The scene must currently be showing or the action will fail.
help_sv2_wait_timeout_ms: Maximum time to wait for the scene to be dismissed, in milliseconds. If the scene is not dismissed within this time, the action will fail. Leave empty or set to 0 to wait indefinitely.
help_sv2_width: The width of the overlay in dp (e.g. 300) or as a percentage of screen width (e.g. 50%). If left empty, the overlay will automatically size itself to fit its content. For different values per orientation, use "portrait,landscape" (e.g. 300,500).
help_sv2_x_position: The horizontal position of the overlay on screen, in dp (density-independent pixels). 0 is the left edge of the screen. Negative values anchor from the right edge instead (e.g. -20 means 20dp from the right). You can also use a percentage of the screen width (e.g. 50%) to center the overlay at that point. Negative percentages anchor from the right (e.g. -25% means 25% from the right edge). For different values per orientation, use "portrait,landscape" (e.g. 300,500).
help_sv2_y_position: The vertical position of the overlay on screen, in dp (density-independent pixels). 0 is the top edge of the screen. Negative values anchor from the bottom edge instead (e.g. -20 means 20dp from the bottom). You can also use a percentage of the screen height (e.g. 50%) to center the overlay at that point. Negative percentages anchor from the bottom (e.g. -25% means 25% from the bottom edge). For different values per orientation, use "portrait,landscape" (e.g. 300,500).
help_system_instructions: System-level instructions sent to the model alongside every prompt.
help_temperature: Sampling temperature (provider-specific range, typically 0-1 or 0-2). Leave blank for the provider default.
help_text_dialog_image: If set, will show an image between the title and text
help_text_dialog_image_max_size:
Size in dip (density-independent pixels). If an image is set you can optionally limit its size with this.

Original image proportions will always be respected.
help_toast_background_color:
Color for the background of the toast.

If not set the current Tasker theme background color will be used.
help_toast_command:
If set, will make the toast interactive and when clicked will call the chosen task.

All the variables available in the task where the toast is created will also be available in the called task.
help_toast_continue_task_right_away: If disabled, will not advance the task to the next action until the toast is gone from the screen.
help_toast_hide_on_click: If enabled, will make the flash go away as soon as it's clicked and the task is launched.
help_toast_icon:
Icon to show on the toast.

If not set, no icon will be shown at all.
help_toast_icon_size:
Size of the icon in dip (density-independent pixels).

Default value is 24.
help_toast_id:
If you set an ID and an existing flash is already showing with the same ID, it'll be replaced by the new one.

If no ID is set, they will appear on top of each other.
help_toast_position:
One of TopLeft, Top, TopRight, Right, BottomRight, Bottom, BottomLeft or Left.

Can optionally provide an offset in dip separated by a comma from the position.

Use the helper for easier setup.
help_toast_show_over_everything:
If enabled, will make the toast show over system UI like the notification tray, lock screen, or even AOD on some devices.

Tasker's accessibility service needs to be on for this to work.

If you want you can disable the 'Continue Task Immediately' option and Tasker will toggle the service on and off when needed automatically.
help_toast_tasker_layout:
Will show the text in a custom Tasker toast instead of using a normal system toast.

You can use HTML to format your text when this option is enabled. For example, you can use <font color=red>Some Text</font> to show some text in red.

Useful to get advanced toast functionality or if your device doesn't support multi-line toasts for example.
help_toast_text_color:
Color for the text of the toast.

If not set, an appropriate text color for the background color will be chosen so that it has good contrast.

If HTML is used in the text and color is sent that way, it'll override this setting just for those parts of the text.
help_toast_timeout_override:
Time in milliseconds the toast should appear on the screen.

If set Will override the normal 'Long' setting above.
help_toast_title: Title to show up above the normal toast text. If not set, only the text will show.
help_toggle_profile:
You can only enable/disable profiles that you have explicitly given a name to.

If a profile isn't showing up here go to your profile list, long click on the profile and give it a name.
help_transition_blur: Blurs out old content and blurs in new content, with the blur radiating from a configurable origin point.
help_transition_card_flip: Flips the container like a card in 3D, revealing new content on the other side.
help_transition_crossfade: Crossfades between old and new content.
help_variable_map_input: The input value that you want to map to the output range based on the input range.
help_widgetv2_ask_to_add: If the widget is not already added to your home screen, show a popup asking you to add it.
help_widgetv2_background_color:
The background color of the whole widget.

If you don't specify text color, it'll automatically be chosen to contrast with this.
help_widgetv2_command_prefix: If set, will prepend "prefix=:=" to all your commands above (where "prefix" is the actual prefix you specify here).
help_widgetv2_commands:
Commands to be ran when you tap on the texts/images above.

Specify one command for each of the text/image, or leave blank to make them not clickable.

These commands will trigger the 'Command' event in Tasker. Check that for more info.
help_widgetv2_custom_layout:
Specify your custom layout here as a JSON structure.

You can also directly use an HTTP/S URL or a file path here.

Make sure to escape any variables you are using inside JSON strings with the 'Variable Convert' action > 'JSON Encode' if needed.

Click below to learn all about Custom Layouts.
help_widgetv2_image_tints:
If you set this, you'll colorize the images above with a single, solid color.

You can specify an image not to be tinted by leaving the value empty.

If you specify less colors than images, the last specified colour will be used for the remainder of the images.
help_widgetv2_images:
Depending on the chosen layout, these images can appear in different places:

- Buttons: are used as the main image for each button
- Media: the first image will be used as the main one on the left. The rest are used as buttons below.
help_widgetv2_material_you_colors: If enabled, will use Material You colors whenever colors are not set explicitly above, which means, the Widget colors will match your wallpaper.
help_widgetv2_number_of_columns:
The number of columns the widget will have to show your data.

For example, if you specify 10 texts and set Number of Columns to 5, you'll get 2 rows with 5 columns each.
help_widgetv2_separator: Character(s) used to separate the values in the multi-value fields (Texts, Images, Tasks, Commands, etc.). For example, set this to a semicolon so a comma can be used inside a value. Leave empty to separate on a comma.
help_widgetv2_sizes:
The size or sizes you want the images to have in dp (Density Independent Pixels).

If you specify less sizes than images, the last specified size will be used for the remainder of the images.
help_widgetv2_tasks:
Tasks to be ran when you tap on the texts/images above.

Specify one task for each of the text/image, or leave blank to make them not clickable.
help_widgetv2_text:
Depending on the chosen layout, these texts can appear in different places:

- Buttons: are used as labels for each button
- Media: is used as the subtitle for the widget
help_widgetv2_text_styles:
Styles for each of the texts above.

If you specify less styles than texts, the last specified style will be used for the remainder of the texts.

A style can be:

- a color in HTML notation or one of the color Material Design tokens (primary, onPrimary, secondary, etc) 
- a number to set the text size in sp
- one of 'sansserif', 'serif', 'monospace', 'cursive' to set the font family
- one of 'left', 'right', 'center', 'start', 'end' to set text alignment
-italic
-bold
-underline
-linethrough

For example, you could set 2 texts with 2 different styles:
- Red, bold text
- Green, italic, underlined text

by setting this to

#FF0000 bold,#00FF00 italic underline.

IMPORTANT: Keep in mind that the title also counts as a text, so the first style you provide is assigned to the title.
ignore_tasker_sets_help: If selected this event will not trigger if Tasker was the app that set the clipboard
input_dates_format_help:
One or more date formats.

For example, yyyy/MM/dd HH:mm will correctly parse a date like 2021/03/05 14:18

You can use a different format for each input.

If there are more inputs than formats, the last format on the list will be used for the remainder of the inputs.
input_dates_help:
One or more dates.

Can be direct values, values from variables or even direct arrays (use %array, not %array()).
java_code_use_tasker_settings_help:
Access a Broader Range of Android APIs

Google Play requires Tasker to be built for recent Android versions (a high 'Target API'). This enhances security but limits access to certain developer functions (APIs).

By checking this, your Java code will be executed by the 'Tasker Settings' app. 'Tasker Settings' has a lower Target API, granting it access to a wider set of Android APIs." b:0,37
keep_existing_variables_help: Will only set the values of variables if they don't already exist by this point in the task
output_dates_format_help:
One or more date formats.

For example, yyyy/MM/dd HH:mm will produce a date like 2021/03/05 14:18

If you specify more than one output format, those formats will be applied to each input, so you'll have all the possible combinations of inputs and formats.

For example, if you have 2 inputs and 3 output formats, you'll get a total of 6 formatted values.

Check out all the possible formats below.
output_dates_format_variable_names_help:
One or more variable names.

Each output will be directly mapped to the variable name available here, e.g., output 1 > variable name 1, output 2 > variable name 2, etc.

Special Behavior for the Last Variable Name:
If there are more output formats than variable names, the last variable name on this list gets special treatment:
1. It will hold its directly mapped output value (e.g., if it's the 2nd variable name, it gets the 2nd output).
2. An array using the same name (e.g., %varname()) will also be created.
 • The first element of this array (%varname(1)) will be the same directly mapped value mentioned above.
 • Any subsequent formatted outputs (those that didn't have their own dedicated variable name) will populate the rest of the array (e.g., %varname(2), %varname(3), etc.).

Example:

Suppose you have 3 Output Formats:
1. dd-MM-yy
2. d
3. yyyy

And 2 Formatted Variable Names:
1. %date
2. %index_day

For an input date of 03-06-25 (assuming input format dd-MM-yy):
• %date (Variable 1) will be: 03-06-25 (from Output Format 1).
• %index_day (Variable 2, the last variable name) will be: 3 (from Output Format 2).
• %index_day() (the array for the last variable name) will contain:
 • %index_day(1) = 3 (from Output Format 2)
 • %index_day(2) = 2025 (from Output Format 3, the remaining unmapped output)
So, %index_day() effectively becomes an array like [3, 2025]." b:170,213 b:791,798 b:820,833 b:868,891
output_dates_help:
Since the input supports both single values and arrays you can use any of these outputs as both single values and arrays.

The number of outputs will depend on how many dates are input.

Additionally, for each Output Format more results will be added for the formated output.

For example, if you have 2 inputs and 3 output formats, you'll get a total of 6 values in the formatted variable output.
pl_check_after_screen_unlock_help: When enabled, Tasker rechecks the WiFi connection on every screen unlock to catch changes that may have been missed while the screen was off. This requires location access, which causes the location indicator to appear. Disable to avoid the location indicator on every unlock.
ppselect_configure_on_import_help: If you enable the option to configure on import you need to fill in a question that the user will be asked when importing this into Tasker. The value of this variable will also be cleared when you export it so that private data is not mistakenly sent to other users.
ppselect_text_profile_variables_help: The variables you add here will be available in the profile's conditions and tasks with the values you specify.
ppselect_text_project_variables_help: The variables you add here will be available in all the profiles and tasks in this project but will not be available in other projects.
ppselect_text_task_variables_help: The variables you add here will be available in this task, with the values you specify
profile_variable_export_value_help:
Under 'Exported Value' if you disable the 'Same as Value' option, you can customize what value gets exported when you share the variable with other users.
You can keep the 'Exported Value' field blank if you want the export to not have a value at all, or you can set the value you wish to always use for exports.
If you enable the 'Save as Value' option, the current variable value will be used when exporting.
profile_variable_immutable_help: If you enable the 'Immutable' option, the variable can be changed in Tasks, but will reset to the value here when the Task ends.
profile_variable_structured_output_help:
Enable the 'Structured Variable' option if the variable is either JSON, HTML or XML so that you can easily read its contents via the dot or square brackets notations.
For example if there's an %json variable and its contents are in the JSON format you could use '%json.info' or '%json[info]' to get the value for the 'info' field.
remote_timeout_help:
The maximum time to wait for the remote action to finish.

If set to 0, the task will continue right away and will not wait for the result.

If set to a positive number, Tasker will wait for the remote action to finish before moving on to the next action. Any local variables set by the remote action will be available in this task too.
settings_accessibility_help_usage_stats_:
If enabled will allow the accessibility service (if enabled) to also detect the current app, even if the App Check Method is set to 'Usage Stats'. This can make app detection faster in most situations, but might not always result in the intended results.

Keep this on if you don't see any anomalies in app detection because it's faster.
settings_action_error_notification_help: If enabled, every time an action ends in error you'll get notified about it unless the action has the 'Continue Task After Error' option enabled.
settings_ask_for_advanced_export_options: If enabled, every time you export a profile or task description, you can select some advanced formatting options for the output, like if it should wrap with backticks or use 4 spaces on every line instead.
settings_ask_for_permission_on_app_exit_:
If enabled, Tasker will check for all the necessary permissions when you exit the app from the main screen or save your setup.

Disable this setting if you have something in your setup that uses a permission that you don't want to remove, but don't want to grant permission for at the moment.
settings_debugging_use_test_servere_help:
If enabled will use a test server to share Tasker projects/profiles/tasks instead of Taskernet.

Use this to test out new server features when available.

If the tests server is offline you may get unexpected errors.
settings_export_light_help:
If enabled, your exports will not contain any data that is not essential for the correct functioning of your projects.

Some helpful info might go away like the names of local variables generated in actions/events/states in some situations, but that's just on the UI level. In the background all the necessary data is still kept.

This has the potential of greatly reducing the size of your backups and Tasker data in general.
settings_help_google_cloud_service_accou: Running actions remotely requires you to setup a Google Cloud and Firebase project.
settings_projects_on_sidebar_help: When on, projects are navigated through the sidebar rail. When off, the sidebar is hidden and your projects appear as entries in the main list instead.
settings_show_all_projects_view_help:
The "All" entry sits at the top of the project sidebar and shows items from every project at once.

Turn this on to add it. When off, the sidebar starts at your projects, since with no projects the "All" view just shows the same thing as the default project.
settings_start_monitor_on_app_open_help: If enabled, as soon as you first open Tasker after a reboot, Tasker's monitor will start right away. If disabled, you'll need to exit Tasker or save your setup for the monitor to start.
structure_global_variable_help:
This variable seems to contain valid %1$s.

Did you know that you can access its contents easily and directly with Tasker?

Want to enable easy structure reading this for this variable now?
structure_prevent_json_smart_search_help: If enabled, Tasker will not automatically search the full JSON structure for the value when reading it.
structure_type_help:
Select the type of data that the variable contains.

If the type doesn't match the data when being read then the type 'None' is assumed instead.
task_inputs_help: Inputs this task expects from apps and AI agents that run it, for example through Android AppFunctions. Give each one the local variable name the task reads and a description of what to put in it. Agents use the descriptions to decide which values to send. Tick Is Array when the input takes several values: the task then reads them as %name1, %name2 and so on.
tip_menu_help: You can press Menu then Info on most screens to access help.
user_handle_select_help:
You can select which profile to toggle by knowing the order you installed it on your device.

Unfortunately there's no way to show a label for each profile since Android doesn't provide it.

For example, if you first installed your Work Profile on your device and later you enabled Private Space, Work Profile will be the first (10) and Private Space will be the second (11).

By default, the first installed profile on your device will be toggled.
